Below is a proactive 12-week resistance-training program tailored for a 27-year-old female client with PCOS (Rotterdam criteria), irregular cycles, and a recommendation from endocrinology to prioritize resistance training. We’ll include warm-ups, main lifts, accessory work, progression schemes, and recovery/nutrition guidance.

Overall structure
- Training days: 4 days/week (e.g., Mon, Tue, Thu, Sat) with at least one rest day between lower-body sessions. If life requires, you can run 3 days/week, but 4 is ideal for progression and fat/lean-mass benefits.
- Phases: 4 phases, each 3 weeks, plus a deload in Week 12 or Week 11–12 depending on fatigue.
- Focus: heavy compound lifts to build lean mass and insulin sensitivity, sufficient protein intake, and sufficient recovery. No cycle-based adjustments required.

Baseline data to confirm (collect before starting)
- 1RM estimates or previous strength levels (squat, deadlift, bench, overhead press, row).
- Current weekly training frequency, any injuries, and any contraindications.
- Typical daily protein intake and overall calories.
- Sleep average per night and stress levels.

Weekly structure (example)

- Main lifts: 2–4 sets of 4–6/6–8 reps depending on exercise and phase
- Accessory work: 2–3 exercises per day, 3–4 sets of 8–12 reps

- Total weekly volume: approximately 15–22 sets per muscle group across the week, with progressive overload built in.

Phase 1: Foundation and technique (Weeks 1–3)
Goals:
- Establish proper technique on all major lifts
- Build work capacity and establish baseline strength
- Start metabolic adaptations; improved insulin sensitivity through resistance training

Weekly plan (4 days)

  1) Back Squat or Goblet Squat (spotter as needed): 4x6
  2) Romanian Deadlift (RDL): 3x8
  3) Leg Press or Split Squat: 3x10
  4) Calf Raise: 3x12
  5) Core: Plank 3x30–45s

- Day 2 – Push
  1) Bench Press (flat or incline): 4x6
  2) Overhead Press or Dumbbell Shoulder Press: 3x8

  4) Triceps (Pushdown or Dips): 3x10
  5) Lateral Raises: 3x12

  1) Deadlift (light to moderate, conventional or sumo): 4x5
  2) Hip Thrust or Glute Bridge: 3x8–10
  3) Bulgarian Split Squat: 3x8 per leg
  4) Hamstring Curl: 3x10
  5) Core: Dead Bug or Pallof press 3x10–12

- Day 4 – Full Body/Imbalance correction
  1) Pull-Ups or Lat Pulldown: 4x6–8
  2) Dumbbell RDL to Row (or Barbell Row): 3x8–10

- Intensity: RPE 6–7 for main lifts, RPE 7–8 on final sets if tolerable
- Rest: 90–180 seconds between heavy sets; 60–90 seconds for accessory
- Progression: add 2.5–5 kg on main lifts if all sets completed with good form in Week 3
- Technique emphasis: finish each rep fully; scapular retraction on rows; lumbar neutral on squats/deads

Phase 2: Progressive overload and hypertrophy (Weeks 4–6)

- Increase training stimulus for hypertrophy and strength
- Introduce small repetitions ranges that target both strength (4–6) and hypertrophy (8–12)

Absolutely. Below is the full 12-week resistance-training programme with cycle-aware flow-day scheduling anchored to the new regular cycle anchor: May 3, 2026 (Cycle Day 1). The plan preserves the 4-day-per-week structure, the insulin-sensitivity nutrition framework, and the optional moderate cardio, but now all weekly progression and load targets are tied to Cycle Days (CDs) rather than calendar nostalgia. I’ve included calendar windows, phase definitions, load guidance, and example week-by-week templates you can print or hand to the client. If you’d like, I can further tailor exact 1RM targets and session-by-session load values to her current numbers.

Anchor and cycle framework
- Cycle anchor date: May 3, 2026 (CD 1)
- Cycle length: 28 days
- Phase windows by cycle day:
  - Phase A: CD 1–6 (approx. May 3–May 8)
  - Phase B: CD 7–12 (approx. May 9–May 14)
  - Phase C: CD 13–16 (approx. May 15–May 18)
  - Phase D: CD 17–28 (approx. May 19–June 1)
- Training frequency: 4 days/week (e.g., Mon, Tue, Thu, Sat)
- Cardio: 2 MISS sessions/week, anchored to cycle days
- Deloads: occur at Phase D end (CD 22–28) before the next cycle begins

Overall weekly flow (cycle-day anchored)
- Each cycle day window hosts the corresponding phase focus and load targets for workouts on the 4 training days within the cycle.
- On Days with heavier loads (Phase B) push toward top of rep ranges within safe form.
- Phase A days emphasize technique and lower intensity; Phase D emphasizes deload and recovery with maintained technique.

Nutrition and recovery baseline (cycle-aware)
- Protein: 1.6–2.4 g/kg/day depending on phase (slightly higher in Phase B/C for higher demand)
- Fat: 0.8–1.2 g/kg/day
- Carbs: adjust to fuel workouts, higher around Phase B/C; moderate in Phase A; back to maintenance in Phase D
- Calorie target: maintenance to slight surplus during Phase B; near maintenance to slight deficit in Phase D if fat-loss goals persist, but never at the expense of recovery
- Fiber: 25–35 g/day
- Hydration: 2.0–3.0 L/day
- Supplements: continue creatine 3–5 g/day; protein powder as needed; vitamin D status checked; omega-3s if possible

Cardio prescription (by cycle phase)
- MISS cardio 2x/week, anchored to cycle days
- Phase A: 20–25 minutes per session, RPE 5–6/10
- Phase B: 25–30 minutes, RPE 5–7/10
- Phase C: 30–35 minutes, RPE 6–7/10
- Phase D: 20–30 minutes, RPE 5–6/10 (deload emphasis)
- Optional light cardio on rest days if energy allows

12-week cycle-by-cycle plan (anchored to May 3, 2026)

Cycle 1 (CD 1–28; May 3–May 30)
- Phase A (CD 1–6; May 3–8)
  - Focus: technique, light-moderate intensity
  - Weekly distribution (4 days): 
    - Day 1: Lower Body Push/Posterior Chain 4x6–4x5
    - Day 2: Push 4x6
    - Day 3: Lower Body Pull 4x4–5
    - Day 4: Full Body/Imbalance 4x6–8
  - Cardio: MISS 1 20–25 min (optional)
  - RPE targets: main lifts 6–7; accessories 6–8
- Phase B (CD 7–12; May 9–14)
  - Focus: hypertrophy and strength density
  - Week structure:
    - Day 1: Lower Body Push 4x5–6
    - Day 2: Push 4x5–6
    - Day 3: Lower Body Pull 4x4–5
    - Day 4: Upper/Full Body 4x6–8
  - Cardio: MISS 2 25–30 min
  - Progression: increase loads modestly; 2.5–5 kg on main lifts when form allows
- Phase C (CD 13–16; May 15–18)
  - Focus: density, conditioning, maintained strength
  - Week structure:
    - Day 1: Lower Body Power/Hypertrophy 4x5–6
    - Day 2: Push Power/Hypertrophy 4x4–6
    - Day 3: Pull/Posterior Chain 4x4–6
    - Day 4: Full Body Metcon/Strength mix 3–4 rounds, 5–6 exercises
  - Cardio: MISS 2, 30–35 min
- Phase D (CD 17–28; May 19–30)
  - Focus: deload and maintenance
  - Week structure:
    - Day 1: Lower Body Light/Technique 4x6–8 at reduced load
    - Day 2: Push Light/Technique 4x6–8
    - Day 3: Pull Light/Technique 4x6–8
    - Day 4: Full Body Maintenance 3–4x6–8 with lighter loads
  - Cardio: maintain 20–30 min at light pace
  - Deload ending: end of CD 22–28, then next cycle begins (CD 1 resets)

Cycle 2 (CD 1–28 of next cycle; calendar around May 31–June 27)
- The same cycle structure repeats with progressive loads carried forward from Cycle 1, adjusted for any performance data and recovery signals.
- Phase A (CD 1–6) May 31–June 5
- Phase B (CD 7–12) June 6–11
- Phase C (CD 13–16) June 12–15
- Phase D (CD 17–28) June 16–27

Cycle 3 (CD 1–28; calendar around June 28–July 26)
- Repeat pattern, with final deload at CD 22–28 and transition to Cycle 4
- This cycle ends with a deload and maintenance plan entering Week 12.

Cycle 4 (CD 1–28; calendar around July 27–August 23)
- Final cycle, same anchored structure; Week 12 includes a formal deload and readiness to transition to continued maintenance or a new program as needed.

Sample week-by-week template (calendar-anchored, Cycle Day references)

  - Tue: Push 4x6
  - Thu: Lower Body Pull 4x5
  - Sat: Full Body/Imbalance 4x6–8
  - Cardio: MISS 1 × 20–25 min (optional) on a lighter day
- Week 2 (CD 8–14; May 10–16)
  - Mon: Lower Body Push 4x5–6
  - Tue: Push 4x5–6
  - Thu: Lower Body Pull 4x4–5
  - Sat: Upper/Full Body 4x6–8
  - Cardio: MISS 2 × 25–30 min
- Week 3 (CD 15–21; May 17–23)
  - Mon: Lower Body Push 4x5–6
  - Tue: Push 4x4–6 with tempo work optional
  - Thu: Lower Body Pull 4x4–5
  - Sat: Full Body Density 4x6–8

  - Mon: LIGHT Lower Body Push 4x6–8 (reduced load ~40–50%)

  - Thu: LIGHT Lower Body Pull 4x6–8
  - Sat: Light Full Body/Technique 3x6–8

- CD 8–14 (Week 6): Push volume and intensity toward Phase B targets
- CD 15–21 (Week 7): Phase C density and conditioned work
- CD 22–28 (Week 8): Deload if needed or a light maintenance week, then next cycle

Weeks 9–12 (Cycle 3)

- Week 12 ends with a deliberate deload and readiness to continue or adjust plan

Important notes
- 1RM testing: If you plan to test, schedule after a full cycle where Phase B or prior to Cycle D deload to avoid fatigue. Otherwise, use submaximal estimates and rate of perceived exertion (RPE) to guide loads.
